editorial.headline: Construction-Material Wholesale Is Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale distribution of clay, lime, cement and glass construction materials is nationally open to foreign investment, but PMA registration in Bali is blocked today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46733 covers the wholesale trade of construction materials made from clay, lime, cement or glass. Its scope is practical and recognisable: pressed roof tiles, traditional roof tiles, pressed and hollow bricks, refractory bricks, floor and wall tiles, concrete tiles, ventilation blocks, bathtubs, toilets, fibre-cement sheets, irrigation pipes and culverts all sit within the activity.

This is a wholesale classification, designed for enterprises trading these building-material categories at any of the declared business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The breadth lies in the material range, from structural and finishing products to sanitaryware and water-related components, while the activity itself remains clearly anchored in wholesale trade.

Nationally, the PMA position is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In ownership terms, the national record permits the activity to be fully foreign-owned. That is the national setting under the cited Presidential Regulations; it is a clear opening for foreign investment in this wholesale activity.

Bali is the decisive exception. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is recorded as Low or Medium-Low across every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The block is tied to the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026: national openness remains real, but it does not translate into a PMA registration route in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the activity can be fully foreign-owned, but Bali blocks its PMA registration route today.
